name: Familial Adult Myoclonic Epilepsy Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Adult Myoclonic Epilepsy

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant family history of adult-onset cortical myoclonus and seizures
Adult onset of cortical myoclonus with or without generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing cortical reflex myoclonus and epileptiform discharges
Identification of pentanucleotide repeat expansions in the SAMD12 gene or other related loci

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history plus adult-onset cortical myoclonus and EEG evidence of cortical reflex myoclonus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical and electrophysiological features are essential.

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of myoclonus
imaging: Brain MRI usually normal or nonspecific cortical atrophy in advanced cases
other: EEG showing cortical reflex myoclonus with giant somatosensory evoked potentials

distinguishingFeatures: Typical EEG with generalized polyspike and wave discharges
No family history of adult-onset myoclonus
Presence of ataxia and cognitive decline
Often associated with metabolic or storage disorders

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
references: Kobayashi K, et al. Familial adult myoclonic epilepsy: clinical and genetic features. Epilepsia. 2019.
Ishiura H, et al. Expansions of intronic TTTCA and TTTTA repeats in benign adult familial myoclonic epilepsy. Nat Genet. 2018.
